definition: To follow rules or standards, or to act the way a group expects.
example: Many newcomers conform to local customs within a few months of moving to a new town.
nuance: To conform is to match a group or standard, sometimes giving up some individuality; to comply is to obey a specific request or order.
prompt: A student transfers to a school where everyone wears the same uniform.
options: Maya chose to conform to the dress code and wore the navy blazer every day.
Maya called the front office to conform that her new blazer had arrived.
Maya decided to conform by wearing a bright orange jacket that no one else owned.
Each morning the students conform in a neat line outside the gym doors.
reasons: Wearing what the school requires is matching its expected standard.
This mixes the word up with confirm, which means to check that something is true.
Standing out from everyone else is the reverse of going along with the group.
The word does not mean to gather or line up; it is a look-alike of form.

practice.prompt: An engineer checks whether a new bridge design meets local building codes.
options: The design will conform to the code by ignoring its rules on steel thickness.
The code will conform to the design so the engineer can skip the inspection.
The design must conform to the building code before construction can begin.
The engineer will conform the meeting time with the inspector by email.
reasons: Ignoring the rules is breaking them, the opposite of meeting them.
This gets the direction backward: the design has to meet the code, not the other way around.
A plan has to meet the official requirements before work can start.
Checking or settling a time is confirming, not matching a standard.
